papers.title: Unbiased Low-Rank Approximation for Repeated Matrix-Vector Multiplication: Stability and Optimal Sampling
papers.abstract: Replacing the matrix in an iteration with random low-rank matrices can reduce the cost of matrix-vector multiplication. However, even if the sampled matrices equal the original matrix in expectation, the expected squared norm of the random iterates may grow while the original iteration converges. Under a fixed rank bound, we study how to choose the distribution of these random matrices to minimize this growth when sampling independently at each step. We derive an exact formula for the optimal asymptotic growth factor and use it to determine when the expected squared norm can converge to zero. We then characterize precisely when a fixed sampling distribution achieves this optimal factor and construct finite-support optimal distributions in every attainable case. These results determine the minimum rank required for stability and provide optimal sampling designs under the prescribed rank constraint.

papers.title: Isomorphism classes and geometric classification of three-dimensional Jordan algebras and the length function
papers.abstract: We investigate the algebraic classification of Jordan algebras of dimensions at most three over arbitrary fields with more than two elements. Our approach combines the theory of nilalgebras and radicals with Peirce, Wedderburn decompositions and the length function. In characteristic two, we adapt the Peirce decomposition to organize the classification, including the field-dependent isomorphism conditions among parametrized families. We also study the varieties of Jordan algebra structures up to dimension three over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two. Besides explicit degenerations and standard arguments, we introduce the alicyclic and characteristic conditions as geometric obstructions to degeneration. We determine the rigid algebras and irreducible components in both dimensions. In dimension three, one component is the nine-dimensional affine space of square-zero products; unlike the other three components, it contains no open orbit.

papers.title: Auslander-type grade conditions and subcategories related to syzygy modules
papers.abstract: The question of when a syzygy module or a module satisfying a Serre condition satisfies the cohomological vanishing conditions known as higher torsionfreeness has been extensively studied. In this paper, we address these questions using grade conditions introduced and studied by Auslander-Bridger and Auslander-Reiten. We also investigate homological conditions on Ext modules and, as an application, give a partial answer over commutative rings to a question of Auslander-Bridger concerning whether higher reflexive modules are higher torsionfree.

papers.title: Positive integral points on Mordell-Schinzel surfaces
papers.abstract: We apply the theory of generalised cluster algebras to classify the finiteness of positive integral points on the class of log K3 surfaces defined by $xyz = G(x,y)$ where $G$ has positive coefficients. We furthermore establish results on Zariski density, number of orbits and asymptotic growth of such points. These provide a Diophantine realisation of the finite-affine-indefinite trichotomy of rank-two root systems.

papers.title: The semiring of spectral duality skeletons: cancellation, characters and factorization
papers.abstract: Weighted dual skeletons are the combinatorial core of spectral duality structures. Their isomorphism classes, under Cartesian product and disjoint union, form a semiring graded by the degree. We identify it completely: a class is determined by its degree, a symmetric element of the group semiring N_0[R] and its number of fixed points. Equivalently, skeletons of a given degree are finite C_2-sets over the C_2-monoid (R,+), these data are their marks, and the semiring is an infinite-monoid analogue of a crossed Burnside semiring. The multiplicative monoid is not cancellative, the only obstruction being that multiplication by a skeleton without fixed points forgets the fixed points; accordingly, the Grothendieck ring has explicit zero divisors. A continuous family of semiring characters, with the degree and the number of fixed points, is a complete invariant, and for commensurable ratios the multiplicative Grothendieck group is described by P\'olya's theorem. The main subject is factorization. The reduced monoid is atomic with bounded lengths, but factorization is not unique, the elasticity is infinite, and even the divisor-closed submonoid with one fixed point is not half-factorial. Without fixed points, every reducible skeleton splits off a single orbit, which gives a criterion by centers, exactly when the number of orbits is 8, 16, a prime or twice a prime. Irreducibility is generic in almost every type. Progression skeletons factor according to mixed-radix number systems, with all factorizations of equal length. Finally, orbit counting gives the dimension of the separatrix and the response rank of products.

papers.title: On the representability of actions of algebras with several bilinear multiplications
papers.abstract: We study the representability of actions in varieties of algebras with $n \geq 1$ not necessarily associative bilinear multiplications. We first prove that, for homogeneous varieties, action accessibility is equivalent to being an Orzech category of interest. For an action accessible, operadic variety we then construct the external weak actor $\mathcal{E}(X)$ of an algebra $X$, an algebra with $n$ bilinear partial operations together with a natural monomorphism encoding the actions on $X$. We characterise the algebras admitting an actor in terms of $\mathcal{E}(X)$, and we deduce an obstruction to action representability: if, for some algebra $X$ with trivial multiplications, $\mathcal{E}(X)$ does not satisfy a multilinear identity of the variety, then the variety is not action representable. Computing the external weak actor explicitly, we obtain that associative and matching dialgebras are weakly action representable but not action representable, and that Poisson algebras, left-right non-commutative Poisson algebras and matching Lie algebras are not action representable. Finally, we introduce the reduced type $(p,q)$ of such a variety and prove that, over a field of characteristic different from $2$, an operadic variety of reduced type $(p,0)$, $(0,q)$ or $(1,1)$ is action representable if and only if it is term equivalent to the variety of Lie algebras or to that of abelian algebras. For the reduced types $(p,0)$ and $(0,q)$, the arguments require no assumption on the cardinality of the field, whereas the case $(1,1)$ requires the field to be infinite.

papers.title: How the eigenvalue region of standardized Laplacians leaves the 2005 polygon
papers.abstract: Let $\Lambda_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of $n\times n$ standardized Laplacian matrices, and let $S_n\subseteq\Lambda_n$ be the polygon introduced in 2005, with upper vertices $\lambda_0=0,\dots,\lambda_{n-1}=1$. It is now known that $\Lambda_n=S_n$, and that $\Lambda_n$ is convex, if and only if $n\le4$. We study how $\Lambda_n$ leaves $S_n$ near an edge $[\lambda_m,\lambda_{m+1}]$, $2(m+1)<n$. First, we prove a switching law for matrices having a boundary point of $\Lambda_n$ as a simple eigenvalue: an explicit switching function on the arcs, built from the left and right eigenvectors and the outward normal, forces maximal weight where positive and zero weight where negative; intermediate weights occur only where it vanishes. Second, we perturb the weights of the arcs $k\to k+m+1$ in the circulant digraph (arcs $k\to k+s$, $1\le s\le m$, plus these arcs with weight $\tau$) that realizes the point $\lambda_m+\tau(\lambda_{m+1}-\lambda_m)$. At second order, the first Fourier harmonic of the perturbation moves the eigenvalue beyond the line of the edge if and only if $\tau<\tau^*_m=\sin(\pi m/n)/(2\cos(\pi/n)\sin(\pi(m+1)/n))$. For even $n$ and $m$, the point with $\tau=\tau^*_m$ is the vertex of $S_{n/2}$ lying on this edge, and digraphs with these arcs only at even $k$ give an explicit eigenvalue path that leaves $S_n$ at $\lambda_m$ and, in all computed cases, ends at this vertex. Third, we give a conjectural, numerically supported picture of $\partial\Lambda_5$: beyond each edge of $S_5$ not incident to $0$ or $1$, $\Lambda_5$ forms a cap bounded by four algebraic arcs, which leaves the edge tangentially at its endpoint adjacent to $0$ or $1$ and rejoins it at $\tau^*_1=(3-\sqrt5)/2$; the rest of the edge lies on $\partial\Lambda_5$. In computations for $n\le8$, a cap returns to its edge smoothly at $\tau^*_m$, at a corner at $\tau^*_m$, or at a corner beyond $\tau^*_m$.

papers.title: Idempotent Ultrafilters and Closed Images of Complete Semilattices
papers.abstract: We prove that every continuous homomorphism from a complete topologized semilattice to a Hausdorff semitopological semilattice has closed image, answering a question of Banakh and Bardyla. The main step is the convergence of idempotent ultrafilters on complete semitopological semilattices. We also prove that, for every complete subsemilattice $X$ of a Hausdorff semitopological semilattice $Y$, the natural order of $X$ is closed in $Y\times Y$. In particular, the natural order of every complete Hausdorff semitopological semilattice $X$ is closed in $X\times X$.

papers.title: Counterexamples to a Cubic Nondegeneracy Conjecture
papers.abstract: Morier-Genoud and Ovsienko conjectured that a cubic Boolean generating function satisfying an ordered separation condition on its second polar must be equivalent to one of two symmetric normal forms. Two infinite families of counterexamples are constructed and proved analytically; both are direct sums of small seeds, and neither is equivalent to the proposed forms even after linear functions are added. The first adjoins a nondegenerate quadratic block to a ternary cubic seed and is distinguished from the proposed forms by the radical of its third polar. This radical determines the associative nucleus of every twisted quasialgebra with the given generating function, so the corresponding algebras are not isomorphic even when the grading is forgotten. The second family consists of direct sums of a five-variable seed and has zero third-polar radical. A criterion for quadratic-block presentations establishes the separation property of the seed; commutation-graph degrees, radical dimensions, and contraction ranks establish non-equivalence in all dimensions of the family.

papers.title: Hammock coordinates for silting subcategories of derived-discrete algebras
papers.abstract: We introduce hammock coordinates to study the combinatorial structure of partial silting configurations in the bounded derived category of a derived-discrete algebra $\Lambda(r,n,m)$. By extracting exact integer inequalities from the Bobi\'nski--Gei\ss{}--Skowro\'nski Hom-hammock formula, we establish a closed-form criterion for pairwise partial silting both within any $\mathcal Z$-component and across distinct components. Using this coordinate framework, we establish three primary results. First, we prove the universal upper bound $|S| \le n+m$ on the cardinality of any partial silting configuration $S$ of $\mathcal Z$-objects ---both globally via Bongartz completion in the silting-discrete setting, and combinatorially within a single component via a $\Sigma^r$-invariant staircase argument. Second, we prove that this bound is universally sharp by constructing an explicit L-shaped partial silting configuration of size $n+m$ for every $\Lambda(r,n,m)$, alongside specialized diagonal configurations. Third, we show that the configuration lattice carries a faithful action of the cyclic group $\mathbb Z/g$ where $g = \gcd(r+m, n-r)$. We conclude by showing a structural obstruction to local determination: pairwise partial silting of consecutive objects in the lattice ordering does not imply global partial silting, due to the strict additivity of a coordinate defect along chains.

papers.title: Centralizers of maps as automorphism groups of Yang--Baxter solutions
papers.abstract: For a partition $X = Y \sqcup Z$ of a set $X$ and an arbitrary map $g \colon Y \to {\rm Hom}_{\rm Set} (Z, \, Z)$, we construct a solution $R_g \colon X \times X \to X \times X$ of the braid equation. We characterize intrinsically the solutions which are isomorphic to some $R_g$ and we give a necessary and sufficient condition for two solutions $R_g$ and $R_{g'}$ to be isomorphic. Consequently, the number of isomorphism classes of the solutions $R_g$ on a set with $n$ elements is $1 + \sum_{k = 1}^{n-1} \widetilde{o} (n - k, \, k)$, where $\widetilde{o} (m, \, k)$ is the number of orbits of the symmetric group $S_m$, acting by conjugation, on the set of multisets with $k$ elements of maps $\{1, \ldots, m\} \to \{1, \ldots, m\}$. This construction is then used to obtain a solution of the braid equation whose automorphism group is exactly the centralizer ${\rm Aut} (f_1, \ldots, f_k)$ of a given family $f_1, \ldots, f_k \colon X \to X$ of maps, $k \geq 1$. For $k = 2$, combined with a result of Agore, Chirvasitu and the author, this gives another proof of the fact that any group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a solution of the braid equation (equivalently, of the set-theoretic Yang--Baxter equation).

papers.title: Interval Replacements of Persistence Modules
papers.abstract: Persistence modules indexed by finite posets arise in topological data analysis. Unlike in the one-parameter case, they need not decompose into interval modules. Interval replacements approximate them by formal differences of interval decomposable modules. Extending earlier work on 2D-grids, we study these replacements for arbitrary compression systems. Different choices can give different interval rank invariants and replacements, including those related to interval resolutions on commutative ladders. Our main results are an explicit formula for interval ranks and an essential-cover theorem. Using Auslander--Reiten theory, we express interval ranks in terms of ranks of matrices formed from the structure maps of the module. The essential-cover theorem recovers each interval rank from a suitable restriction of the module. The replacement construction preserves the corresponding interval rank invariant, which recovers the usual rank invariant on segments. Essential covers also give a sufficient condition for two compression systems to yield the same invariant. For total compression, the invariant coincides with the generalized rank invariant of Kim and M\'emoli. On 2D-grids, essential covers recover the zigzag formula of Dey, Kim, and M\'emoli for this invariant.

papers.title: Catalan Semirings
papers.abstract: We study Catalan semirings, which are additively idempotent semirings whose multiplicative semigroups belong to a natural family of transformation monoids known as Catalan monoids. There are two kinds of Catalan semirings, whose properties differ substantially. We address the Finite Basis Problem for individual Catalan semirings of each kind and their representations by Boolean triangular matrices. Furthermore, we characterize the varieties and pseudovarieties generated by all Catalan semirings of each kind.

papers.title: Equivariant Cleft Extensions and Singular Equivalences
papers.abstract: We study the equivariant lifting of cleft extensions of abelian categories and its impact on singularity categories. Specifically, we establish the necessary framework for lifting a cleft extension to a G-equivariant cleft extension. Furthermore, we prove that a restriction functor associated to a cleft extension induces a singular equivalence if and only if its equivariant counterpart does. As a concrete application, we demonstrate that the skew group ring of a $G$-equivariant $\theta$-extension is isomorphic to a $\widehat{\theta}$-extension of the base skew group ring, allowing us to lift singular equivalences for these structures.

papers.title: Bipartite solutions of the set-theoretic Yang--Baxer equation
papers.abstract: We introduce a new class of unitary set-theoretic Yang--Baxter solutions, called \emph{bipartite} solutions. This class, which is purely combinatorial in nature, forms a full subcategory of $\mathcal{LYB}$, the category of Lyubashenko type solutions of Agore, Chirvasitu and the author, and is particularly amenable to explicit classification results. We give an intrinsic necessary and sufficient condition for a solution of the Yang--Baxter equation to be isomorphic to a bipartite solution, we settle the isomorphism problem within this class and, as an application, we determine their automorphism groups. If $X$ is a finite set with $|X| = n$, the number of isomorphism classes of bipartite solutions on $X$ is $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1 + \sum_{m=2}^{n} \bigl( o(m, n-m) - 1 \bigr)$, where $o(m, k)$ denotes the number of orbits of the symmetric group $S_m$ acting by conjugation on the $k$-element multisets of elements of $S_m$. The paper also offers a comparative study: for small $|X| = n$ we count, up to isomorphism, all set-theoretic Yang--Baxter solutions on $X$, together with five distinguished families of solutions. Throughout the range we were able to compute, the class $\mathcal{LYB}$ accounts for a large share of all bijective and of all non-degenerate solutions, strikingly close to the total.

papers.title: On the lower bound of the refined Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture: proof of the cases S_{6,3} and S_{7,3} for 3x3 matrices
papers.abstract: For Hermitian matrices $\alpha,\beta$ let $\A_{n,m}(e^\alpha,e^\beta)$ be the average of the traces of all words with $n$ letters $e^\alpha$ and $m$ letters $e^\beta$. The refined Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture contains the lower bound $\A_{n,m}(e^\alpha,e^\beta)\ge\Tr e^{n\alpha+m\beta}$ (Tr denotes the trace), which for $n=m=1$ is the Golden--Thompson inequality. We prove this lower bound for all $n+m\le7$ when the matrices have size at most three, and for $\min(n,m)\le2$ in every dimension. In all these cases we prove the stronger inequality $\A_{n,m}(A,B)\ge\Tr(A^{n/m}B)^m$ for positive semidefinite $A,B$, or its mirror image with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged; the lower bound of the refined conjecture follows from the Araki--Lieb--Thirring inequality. The cases with three letters $B$ in dimension three, $(n,m)=(3,3)$ and $(4,3)$, are reduced by an exact identity and the inequality of arithmetic and geometric means to a polynomial inequality in two variables, which is certified in exact rational arithmetic by Bernstein expansion on three boxes. The certificate is a short program in the ancillary files.

papers.title: A Non-linearizable Action of $S_3$ on Free Metabelian Lie and Associative Algebras
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be the free metabelian Lie algebra of rank $4$ over the field of complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$. We construct a non-linearizable action of the symmetric group $S_3$, the smallest nonabelian group, on $M$ by automorphisms. We also construct a non-linearizable action of $S_3$ on free metabelian associative algebras of rank $4$.

papers.title: Primary components and large prime factors of cyclotomic values
papers.abstract: Let $\Phi_r(a,b)$ denote the homogeneous cyclotomic value. For sufficiently large $A$, uniformly for $1/2\leq B\leq A$, $r\geq3$ and $Z\geq2$, the number of coprime pairs in $(A,2A]\times(B,2B]$ whose greatest prime factor $P(\Phi_r(a,b))$ is at most $Z$ is $O(AB/\varphi(r)+\sqrt{r/\varphi(r)}\,\pi(Z;r,1))$, where $\pi(Z;r,1)$ counts primes at most $Z$ congruent to $1$ modulo $r$. If $n=n(A)\to\infty$ through positive integers and $1\leq H(A)=o(\log A)$, then $P(a^{2^n}+1)>2^nAH(A)$ for almost all $a\in(A,2A]$, and $P(a^{2^n}+b^{2^n})>2^nA^2H(A)$ for almost all coprime pairs in $(A,2A]^2$, with no further restriction on $n$. For every fixed $\alpha>0$ and every $r\geq A^\alpha$, pairwise distinct primitive prime divisors of $\Phi_r(a)$ can be selected for all but $O_\alpha(A^{1-c_\alpha})$ bases in $(A,2A]$, where $c_\alpha>0$. For coprime positive integers $a,b$ with $\max(a,b)\geq2$ and $r\geq3$, put $C=\Phi_r(a,b)$ and $S=\varphi(r)^2\log\max(a,b)$. Uniformly as $S\to\infty$, $\max_{p\mid C}p^{v_p(C)}\geq(5/16-o(1))S$. For every positive function $h(S)\to\infty$, $\sum_{p\mid C,\;p^{v_p(C)}>S/h(S)}v_p(C)\log p =(1-o(1))\log C$ uniformly in the same limit.

papers.title: Complete Bernstein functions and real powers of P-matrices
papers.abstract: We classify the nonzero complete Bernstein functions whose matrix functions preserve every real P-matrix in every order. They are precisely $f(z)=a+bz$, with $a,b\ge0$ and $a+b>0$, and $f(z)=a+cz/(z+s)$, with $a\ge0$ and $c,s>0$. For each fixed order $n\ge4$, the preservers vanishing at zero are exactly $cz$ and $cz/(z+s)$; every other such function admits a strictly totally positive counterexample. For a finite positive measure $\mu$ on $(0,\infty)$, put $g(z)=\int z/(z+s)\,\mu(ds)$ and $M_t=\int s^t\,\mu(ds)$. In every fixed order $n\ge4$, a finite constant shift restores preservation on all real P-matrices if and only if $M_{r_n}$ and $M_{-r_n}$ are finite, where $r_n=\lfloor n/2\rfloor-1$. Every $a>c_n\sqrt{M_{r_n}M_{-r_n}}$ is sufficient, with $c_n$ depending only on $n$. A complete Bernstein function vanishing at zero admits a possibly different repairing constant in every order exactly when it is linear, or is a pure kernel mixture with all positive and negative integer moments finite. For principal real powers, the preserving exponents are $\mathbb R$ in order one, $[-1,1]$ in orders two and three, and $\{-1,0,1\}$ in every higher order. An explicit rational determinant-one totally positive family gives negative principal minors uniformly on prescribed compact subsets of $(-1,0)\cup(0,1)$.

papers.title: Classification of three-dimensional Leibniz dialgebras with two-dimensional annihilator
papers.abstract: A Leibniz dialgebra is a vector space with two bilinear products $\dashv$ and $\vdash$ satisfying the dialgebra analogue of the right Leibniz identity. This notion is obtained by the same standard procedure that turns the associative identity into the axioms of Loday's associative dialgebras. In particular, $(\mathcal{DL},\dashv)$ is a right Leibniz algebra, so a Leibniz dialgebra is a Leibniz algebra together with a second, compatible product. This paper recalls the definition of Leibniz dialgebras and continue the algebraic classification of three-dimensional complex Leibniz dialgebras. This paper describes up to isomorphism all Leibniz dialgebras $(\mathcal{DL},\dashv,\vdash)$ for which the Leibniz algebra $(\mathcal{DL},\dashv)$ is isomorphic to one of the algebras $\mathcal{L}_{8}(\alpha)$, $\mathcal{L}_9$, $\mathcal{L}_{10}$, $\mathcal{L}_{11}$ of the classification of three-dimensional complex Leibniz algebras. The result consists 18 families of pairwise non-isomorphic Leibniz dialgebras, nine of which depend on a complex parameter.

papers.title: Completing the classification of Hopf superalgebras of dimension up to 10
papers.abstract: We introduce a family of semisimple Hopf superalgebras obtained from abelian extensions. Using this family and bosonization, we complete the classification of Hopf superalgebras of dimension up to 10 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We also determine the duals of the semisimple classes with nonzero odd part and give tables of the complete classification.

papers.title: Quantum Generalized Cluster Algebras from Scattering Diagrams: Positivity and Mutation
papers.abstract: We construct generalized quantum cluster scattering diagrams over a ring of formal reciprocal exchange coefficients, for compatible seeds satisfying \(\widetilde B^T\Lambda=[I_n\mid0].\) A central lattice extension records the roots of the exchange polynomials as independent degrees. Applying Davison--Mandel positivity in this extension and proving a positive cylinder projection theorem yields positive wall factorizations and theta coefficients in the root variables. Their regular classical limits recover generalized cluster scattering diagrams. Nonvanishing under classical specialization, together with control of the mutated positive monoids, gives quantum mutation compatibility. The resulting scattering atlas has the generalized cluster fan, and every reachable cluster monomial is a theta function. Classical detection of theta coefficients gives a geometric proof of the Laurent phenomenon, with positivity after adjoining the polynomial roots. Evaluation of the exchange coefficients recovers the generalized quantum cluster algebras with this normalization. The Fock--Goncharov mutation product becomes a wall-crossing action, identifying extended \(g\)-vectors with leading theta exponents and \(F\)-polynomials with the coefficient factors on their right. Constructing these polynomials before evaluation gives the separation formula for arbitrary prescribed reciprocal Laurent polynomial coefficients, without requiring positivity at \(t=1.\) Positivity in the roots is distinguished throughout from positivity in the exchange coefficients.

papers.title: Local superderivations of Block Lie superalgebras $S(q)$
papers.abstract: We prove that every even or odd local superderivation of the Block Lie superalgebra $S(q)$ is a superderivation for every $q\in\mathbb{C}$, with both basis indices ranging over $\mathbb{Z}$. The superderivations used in the local condition have the same parity as the map. The proofs use the known description of homogeneous superderivations, bracket computations, and coefficient comparisons.

papers.title: Partial coactions of Hopf algebras on nonunital algebras and categories
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and investigate partial coactions of a Hopf algebra on an associative, possibly nonunital algebra and on $\Bbbk$-linear categories. We prove that every partial coaction has a globalization in a broad sense. We study in detail the case of a partial coaction on an algebra with local units; we prove that such a coaction is always induced from a global coaction, and we show that there exists a naturally associated $\Bbbk$-linear category endowed with a partial coaction.

papers.title: Varieties of associative algebras with slow central codimension growth
papers.abstract: Central codimensions measure the dimensions of spaces of multilinear polynomials modulo those taking values in the center of an algebra. We classify associative algebras over a field of characteristic zero whose central codimensions grow at most linearly. The classification is given up to equality of polynomial identities, in terms of explicit generating algebras and an equivalent finite exclusion criterion. We also give a direct structural characterization of the bounded case. As a consequence, we determine the five varieties of quadratic central codimension growth whose proper subvarieties all have at most linear central growth. As an application of the bounded-growth classification, we characterize algebras graded by an arbitrary finite group whose graded central codimensions are bounded. Up to graded PI-equivalence, these are direct sums of commutative and nilpotent graded algebras, possibly together with the Grassmann algebra on two generators endowed with the trivial grading.

papers.title: The Yangian associated with the binary tree
papers.abstract: In this article, we give three candidates for a definition of the Yangian associated with the binary tree $X^*$ and the group $Aut(X^*)$ consisting of automorphisms of $X^*$ which preserve the tree structure. The first candidate has the Schur-Weyl duality with one kind of an extension of the degenerate affine Hecke algebra. The second and third ones have a homomorphism corresponding to the wreath recursion.

papers.title: RaFH and CRaFH superalgebras: Frobenius forms, representation theory and respectability
papers.abstract: We introduce \emph{RaFH superalgebras}, which are Rees affine Frobenius Hecke superalgebras. These algebras are defined by generators and relations, using \emph{Frobenius-tensor superalgebras} to axiomatise tensor powers of Frobenius superalgebras together with their copairing elements. The RaFH superalgebras include, as special cases, the affine and degenerate affine Hecke algebras of type $A$, the affine Sergeev superalgebras, the affine wreath product algebras and quantum affine wreath algebras, as well as the recently introduced quantum wreath product algebras in the special case of the superflip braiding. We study the RaFH superalgebras from both structural and representation theoretic points of view. We prove a basis theorem for the RaFH superalgebras, construct universal Jucys--Murphy elements, and classify their simple modules over an algebraically closed field via atomic superalgebras, which are smaller RaFH superalgebras of Hecke, Clifford or wreath type. We then study \emph{CRaFH superalgebras}, which are the cyclotomic quotients of the RaFH superalgebras. We construct bases for these superalgebras, and compute the Gram determinants of natural trace forms, and use these to determine when these superalgebras are symmetric or Frobenius. To study the representation theory of the CRaFH superalgebras, we introduce the \emph{respectable algebras}, which is a vast generalisation of cellular algebras, standardly based algebras and finite dimensional affine cellular algebras, and give many examples illustrating their variety and ubiquity. We then show that CRaFH superalgebras are respectable algebras with weight poset given by multipartitions that are coloured by the representations of the underlying Frobenius algebra. This result can be viewed as a far-reaching generalisation of Murphy's bases into the setting of CRaFH algebras.

papers.title: Extensions at Nonzero p-Characters for Cartan-Type Lie Algebras
papers.abstract: For restricted simple Cartan-type Lie algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p\ge5$, the reduced enveloping algebra at every nonzero $p$-character is a matrix algebra over a terminal symmetric corner, and this corner determines the extensions. Central-socle traces recover its radical and its simple factors, and the first radical layer determines the degree-one extensions. For the Witt algebra $W(1;1)$, at even height $2\le h\le p-3$, the unique simple module has self-extension dimension $\min\{p-h-2,h+2\}$. At height two in characteristic seven, we present the Yoneda algebra as an eight-dimensional symmetric algebra tensored with a polynomial algebra on three central degree-two classes. An equivariant Tate resolution and cocycle identities prove the presentation in all degrees.

papers.title: Every group is the automorphism group of a set-theoretic solution of the Yang--Baxter equation
papers.abstract: We give an affirmative answer to the \emph{abstract group problem} for the category $\YB$ of all set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter (YB) equation: every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a YB-solution, which can be chosen on a finite set if the group is finite. In the terminology of L\'aszl\'o Babai, this means that the category $\YB$ is \emph{universal} and \emph{finitely universal}, which is an analogue of Frucht's classical theorem for graphs. Furthermore, the YB-solutions can be chosen within three very small classes: the solutions of the Frobenius-Separability equation, the solutions of the Baaj--Long--Skandalis equation and the recently introduced bipartite solutions. The proof is based on new constructions which associate to any graph a YB-solution in each of these classes, with the same automorphism group as the graph. Explicit YB-solutions with automorphism groups $C_n$, $S_n$, $D_n$ and $Q_8$ are given, as well as a unitary YB-solution, constructed directly from a field $K$, whose automorphism group is ${\rm Aut} (K)$.

papers.title: Embedding a Quantum Rank Two Quadric in a Quantum $\mathbb{P}^3$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we classify connected graded quadratic Artin-Schelter regular (AS-regular, henceforth) algebras of global dimension four that have a Hilbert series the same as that of the polynomial ring on four generators and that map onto a twisted homogeneous coordinate ring of a rank-two quadric. A twisted homogeneous coordinate ring is a construction that was defined by Artin, Tate, and Van den Bergh in \cite{ATV1, ATV2, AVdB1990} in the context of the classification of AS-regular algebras of global dimension three. In \cite{SV99,VVr}, the authors classified AS-regular algebras of global dimension four that map onto the twisted homogeneous coordinate ring of a rank-three and a rank-four quadric, respectively. We expand on their work to include the case of coordinate rings of a rank-two quadric.
